name: Rebaptism
overview: Scripture clearly teaches that baptism is an essential act of obedience following belief and repentance, as seen in Jesus' command to baptize disciples in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19) and the promise of salvation linked to belief and baptism (Mark 16:16). The early church practiced baptism as a response to repentance and reception of the gospel, demonstrated by Peter's call to be baptized for the remission of sins and receiving the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:38), and the immediate baptism of thousands who embraced the message (Acts 2:41). The account in Acts 10:48 further confirms baptism in the name of the Lord as a normative practice, while Acts 19:1 hints at the need to ensure proper baptismal understanding among disciples. Together, these passages emphasize that baptism is a one-time, gospel-affirming act that follows genuine faith and repentance.
